answers.topic: Splitting Sales Representatives: work order card, height of the box around the Sales Representative field
answers.question:
When the mouse is over the Sales Representative field on the work order card, a box appears around it. How tall should the box be?
(a) Suggested, as the newest document (the feature spec, version 8 of 14 Oct) says: exactly the height of the Lead Technician and Service Advisor boxes (the developers measure 42 px today). The 44 px in the Jira story is out of date.
(b) 44 px, as the Jira story says.
answers.what_we_knew: Feature spec: the box sits "at the same height as those two fields and the same left edge". The Jira story still says "at the same 44px height". The tech plan builds to the existing 42 px.
answers.answer_verbatim: (a) as the feature spec: same height as Lead Technician and Service Advisor (42 px). The Jira story will be refreshed.
answers.where_found: PRD v8 (14 Oct 2026) S1-R4; Jira SV-11265 (Story 1); tech plan §0

answers.topic: Splitting Sales Representatives: work order card and Audit Log, a person who no longer exists or belongs to another organization
answers.question:
If the person saved in a Sales Representative field no longer exists in the shop (or belongs to another organization), what should show?
On the work order card:
(a) "Unassigned".
(b) "(Inactive)" with no name.
(c) Nothing (an empty field).
In the work order's Audit Log:
(d) "Unassigned".
(e) "Unknown".
answers.what_we_knew: The feature spec covers only the printout: "A side whose staff member no longer exists prints as Unassigned. A row never reads a bare "(Inactive)"." The tech plan has the card show "(Inactive)" with no name in one place and an empty field in another, and the log show "Unknown".
answers.answer_verbatim: 5. Card: (a) "Unassigned". Audit Log: (d) "Unassigned". Same as the printout.

answers.topic: Splitting Sales Representatives: work order card, two people editing the same work order
answers.question:
Two people (or two browser tabs) have the same work order open. Tab A adds the Parts field. Tab B still shows one field and picks a person. What should happen?
(a) Tab B's choice wins and the Parts field disappears (what the tech plan builds).
(b) Tab B's choice changes only the Labor side, and the Parts field stays.
(c) Tab B is told to reload the work order.
answers.what_we_knew: Feature spec: "A side is never refilled on its own." The tech plan says this holds for every user, "including a stale tab", and that the screen always says whether the work order is split when it saves.
answers.answer_verbatim: 6. (a) Tab B's choice wins and the Parts field disappears: the later save wins, as everywhere else.

answers.topic: Splitting Sales Representatives: customer, deactivating a staff member who is a customer's sales representative
answers.question:
When a staff member's account is deactivated, what happens to the customers they are the sales representative for?
(a) Suggested, as the newest document (the feature spec, version 8 of 14 Oct) says: they are removed from every customer field they hold; the customer's other fields keep their people; reactivating does not put them back. The warning line "Their customer assignments will stay where they are." must then change: please give the new wording.
(b) Keep today's rule: they stay on their customers, the warning stays as it is, and the feature spec's rule is dropped.
(c) Remove them, but put them back if the person is reactivated.
answers.what_we_knew: Feature spec: "Deactivating a staff member's account removes them from every customer field they hold." The Sales By Representative spec (12 Oct; this part unchanged since August) still says assignments "are not modified by deactivation", the warning says "Their customer assignments will stay where they are.", reactivating brings them back, and the Assignments export lists deactivated people with "Rep is active?" = "No". Today the product keeps them (checked on 4 Aug 2026).
answers.answer_verbatim: 12. (a) as the feature spec: removed from every customer field they hold, not put back on reactivation. New warning line: "They will be removed as sales representative from {n} customers."
answers.where_found: PRD v8 S4-R20; Sales By Representative spec v28 (12 Oct 2026) S13-R4, S13-R10, S13-R11, S13-E1, S13-E3, S15-R2, S15-R6

answers.topic: Splitting Sales Representatives: Sales By Representative, who gets the odd cent when a discount is shared
answers.question:
When a whole-invoice discount does not split evenly between the Labor and Parts rows, who gets the odd cent? Example: labor $100.00, parts $200.00, discount ($1.00); the exact parts share is ($0.666...).
(a) Parts is rounded to the nearest cent, ($0.67), and Labor gets the rest, ($0.33); Labor gets an extra cent only on an exact half cent (what the tech plan builds).
(b) Parts is rounded down to ($0.66) and the left-over cent goes to Labor, ($0.34).
(c) Another rule (please describe).
answers.what_we_knew: Feature spec: "A cent left over by rounding the share goes to the Labor row." The tech plan rounds to the nearest cent and keeps only a tie cent with Labor. The Sales By Representative spec rounds displayed values half up, but that is about display, not about sharing. Both worked examples in the feature spec add up.
answers.answer_verbatim: 21. (a) Parts is rounded to the nearest cent and Labor gets the rest; Labor gets the extra cent only on an exact half cent.
answers.where_found: PRD v8 S5-R6, S5-R7; tech plan §8.2; Sales By Representative spec v28 §3 (rounding)

answers.topic: Splitting Sales Representatives: Sales By Customer, what "remembered from before the release" means

answers.topic: Splitting Sales Representatives: sentences in the Sales By Representative spec that were not updated
